title: On the General Sylvester-type Construction of Hadamard Matrices and Their Modifications
abstract: Using the ideas of the concatenation construction of codes over the $q$ -ary alphabet, we previously modified in [1] the well-known generalized Sylvester-type construction of Hadamard matrices. The new general construction is based on two collections of initial Hadamard matrices. Specifically, this construction involves $m$ Hadamard matrices of order $k$ and $k$ Hadamard matrices of order $m$ . These initial matrices are not necessarily distinct. As a result, we obtain a Hadamard matrix of order $km$ . The new construction provides numerous possibilities for constructing new Hadamard matrices with various ranks and kernel dimensions, including, in particular, regular Hadamard matrices. In the present paper, we determine sufficient conditions for the resulting matrix to be linear or regular.

title: Quantum Key Distribution Based Physical Layer Security Applied in Complex Modulation Formats for Optical Fiber Links
abstract: A Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) based Physical Layer Security (PLS) scheme (QKD-PLS) for optical fiber links is proposed and evaluated. In detail, a novel amplitude and phase scrambling technique for exploiting and seamlessly integrating high key rate QKD for the encryption of the modulation parameters of conventional complex modulation schemes like M-ary Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (M-QAM) and Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) is described. The technique masks the information at the bit level and blocks unauthorized access to the higher layer encrypted bitstream. Scrambling is applied to both the preamble (pilot) and payload segments of the transmission frame, to prevent the eavesdroppers from performing vital receiver functions such as frame synchronization and channel estimation. Additionally, a practical Key Management System (KMS) which takes care of all synchronization processes is developed and introduced. Experimental transmission scenario in fiber links is also presented and depicts the efficacy of the QKD-PLS. Moreover, another advantage of QKD exploitation to the proposed solution comes from the application of kbps-rate QKD keys which feed pseudo-random number generators, to modify the broadband modulation symbols in one-time pad, therefore significantly improving data protection.

title: Deciphering interventional dynamical causality via Kolmogorov–Arnold networks
abstract: Identifying causal relationships from observational time-series data is a central challenge in understanding complex dynamical systems. However, few existing methods attempt to capture the intuitive human understanding of causality: that an intervention on one variable leads to a subsequent change in another. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces a causal discovery method named Intervened TaylorKAN (ITK), which simulates controlled experiments within reconstructed systems. Specifically, we leverage the recently emerging Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) with Taylor series as activation functions to construct a surrogate model that faithfully replicates the original system's dynamics. The core of ITK involves applying targeted interventions on this reconstructed system and observing the responses in other variables, thereby providing more intuitive causal inferences. We evaluated ITK's performance through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets. Results demonstrate that ITK achieves high accuracy on synthetic data with known causal structures, confirming its validity. When applied to real-world data, ITK produces reasonable and interpretable causal conclusions, highlighting its potential to decipher causal relationships in complex natural systems.

title: LIA-FL: A containerised federated learning platform for AIoT time-series forecasting
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without requiring the exchange of raw data, making it suitable for distributed Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) environments. This paper presents LIA-FL, a containerised software platform for deploying and orchestrating FL workflows using Docker, Docker Compose, MQTT-based communication, TensorFlow/Keras models, and local SQLite storage. The platform provides federated nodes, an aggregation server implementing the Federated Averaging algorithm, model persistence, fragmented model-weight transmission, integrity checking, and structured logging facilities. The software is demonstrated through a meteorological forecasting use case involving distributed weather stations organised into groups of contextually similar nodes, showing its applicability to reusable AIoT scenarios.

title: Minimax–least-squares composite polynomial approximation of ReLU for homomorphic neural network inference
abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables privacy-preserving neural network inference over encrypted data, but non-arithmetic operations such as ReLU cannot be directly evaluated. A common approach is to approximate ReLU using composite minimax polynomials for the sign function, which minimize the worst-case error over a prescribed approximation interval. However, this criterion does not reflect the actual distribution of ReLU inputs in neural networks. In this paper, we propose a minimax–least-squares composite polynomial approximation for FHE-friendly ReLU evaluation. The proposed method preserves the composite structure of existing minimax-based approaches while optimizing the last polynomial by least squares to minimize the mean squared error (MSE) under the profiled input distribution of each ReLU layer. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves lower ReLU approximation MSE than existing methods and improves classification accuracy on ResNet models by 3.51 percentage points on average at no additional cost over existing composite methods, with the largest gains for deep networks.

title: Accelerating A*-Based Algorithms for Decoding Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes represent a promising approach for error correction in quantum computing. The recently proposed Tesseract decoder uses the A* search algorithm that guarantees finding the most likely error pattern. However, practical implementations of Tesseract often involve an extremely large graph, and the inherently sequential nature of the search results in high computational overhead and long runtime. To improve decoding efficiency, we propose a two-stage decoding framework. First, a belief propagation (BP) decoder efficiently processes the syndrome. This step generates hard decisions (a binary error vector) and soft information (per-qubit confidence levels). In non-convergent BP cases, a gating mechanism examines the BP decoder's output to identify and filter out qubits with oscillating confidence values. In these cases, the refined output serves as input to Tesseract, which then attempts to identify and correct any residual errors. This hybrid approach leverages the high speed of BP decoding and delegates the more challenging decoding instances to Tesseract. Numerical results demonstrate a substantial reduction in overall decoding complexity while maintaining the logical error rate (LER) of the stand-alone Tesseract. Across all tested physical error rates, the proposed method achieves at least 5x reduction in the number of expanded nodes in the Tesseract, with a peak reduction of nearly 15x at a physical error rate of p = 0.05 for the [[126, 12, d < 11]] T1 code, and approximately 8.8x at p = 0.05 for the [[72, 12, 6]] bicycle bivariate (BB) code.

title: Median-of-Means as an Extremal Convex Estimator and a Nonconvex Route to the Trimmed Oracle
abstract: We revisit median-of-means estimation from a deterministic optimization viewpoint and develop a family of block-Lp estimators for robust learning with heavy-tailed and adversarially corrupted data. In a block contamination model with at least a fraction 1 minus epsilon of good blocks, we first show that every convex block M-estimator has worst-case robustness constant at least 1 divided by 1 minus 2 epsilon. This matches the classical median-of-means bound and proves that the trimmed-block oracle constant 1 divided by 1 minus epsilon cannot be attained within the convex class. We then introduce a nonconvex block-Lp family for p between 0 and 1 and derive finite-sample deterministic robustness bounds for all global minimizers. As p decreases from 1 toward 0, these bounds continuously approach the trimmed-block oracle constant. For sufficiently small p, the global minimizers coincide with those of the oracle under a mild separation condition. We also show that the block-Lp objectives have a benign landscape, with all local minima remaining close to the truth and no bad basins. Combining these results with block-level concentration yields sub-Gaussian deviation bounds under finite 2 plus delta moments and high-dimensional extensions to robust mean estimation and sparse regression.

title: A General Construction of Codes from Drinfeld Modules
abstract: We construct additive rank-metric and sum-rank-metric codes from Drinfeld modules by restricting bounded-degree morphisms to prime-to-characteristic torsion. For supersingular Drinfeld modules of rank $r$ in characteristic $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree $d$, the stabilization formula for morphism spaces yields rank-metric codes of $\mathbb{F}_q$-dimension $mrt-c$ and minimum distance $r-t+1$, where $c=r(r-1)(d-1)/2$. Simultaneous restriction to $\ell$ distinct degree-$m$ torsion modules gives additive sum-rank codes of the same dimension and minimum distance at least $\ell r-t+1$. Their normalized Singleton defects tend to zero, while in characteristic $(T)$ the module $ϕ_T=τ^r$ makes the defect vanish and produces an explicit MSRD family. We identify this family with a skew Chinese remainder theorem code supported on central skew polynomials and prove that its poly-skew weight is exactly $m$ times its sum-rank weight. This gives a specialized Singleton-type bound and a polynomial-time unique decoder up to the full sum-rank unique-decoding radius. We also derive a Welch-Berlekamp-type filter equation for the general supersingular sum-rank construction; it becomes an effective decoder whenever bases of the relevant morphism spaces and the restriction maps are computable.

title: Nonparametric inference for density-dependent McKean--Vlasov diffusions
abstract: The present research is devoted to the nonparametric estimation of a density-dependent drift coefficient in a multivariate McKean--Vlasov diffusion from independent observations at a common time, as well as the stationary density. Under certain assumptions on the (known) potential, we reduce the problem to the one-dimensional one and construct a sieve maximum-likelihood estimator based on sparse ReQU neural networks subject to structural and Hölder constraints. Using the endpoint-adapted graded approximation, we achieve the rate of $\left(b_n\log n/n\right)^{2(β+1)/(2β+3)}$ for the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the true and estimated stationary densities, with $b_n$ being at most a logarithmic factor. Similarly, it is shown that the constructed estimator for the drift coefficient converges to the true one at the rate of $\left(b_n\log n/n\right)^{β/(2β+3)}$ in the $L^2$-metric. A matching Assouad lower bound proves minimax optimality of this bound up to logarithmic factors.

title: HELIOS: From midnight to noon, continuous outdoor urban scene relighting
abstract: Modifying the illumination of driving images is a fundamental challenge, as most datasets are captured at specific times of day. Existing methods rely on synthetic data or paired multi-illumination supervision, which limits their generalization to the diverse and challenging conditions of real-world scenarios. To address this, we propose HELIOS, a novel image relighting approach that relies on unlabeled real-world datasets without requiring any paired images for training. Our approach integrates albedo-based conditioning into a cycle-consistent diffusion pipeline to prevent identity collapse and ensure accurate domain translation. To handle low-visibility nighttime conditions, we introduce a robust albedo distillation strategy that transfers structural stability from the daytime domain. Additionally, we replace traditional text prompts with a fine-grained control mechanism based on GPS-derived solar angles, enabling smooth and continuous lighting manipulation across the day-night cycle. Through extensive evaluation and a user study, we demonstrate that HELIOS produces structurally consistent and realistic results in both night-to-day and day-to-night tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art methods.

evidence.title: HELIOS: From midnight to noon, continuous outdoor urban scene relighting
evidence.abstract: Modifying the illumination of driving images is a fundamental challenge, as most datasets are captured at specific times of day. Existing methods rely on synthetic data or paired multi-illumination supervision, which limits their generalization to the diverse and challenging conditions of real-world scenarios. To address this, we propose HELIOS, a novel image relighting approach that relies on unlabeled real-world datasets without requiring any paired images for training. Our approach integrates albedo-based conditioning into a cycle-consistent diffusion pipeline to prevent identity collapse and ensure accurate domain translation. To handle low-visibility nighttime conditions, we introduce a robust albedo distillation strategy that transfers structural stability from the daytime domain. Additionally, we replace traditional text prompts with a fine-grained control mechanism based on GPS-derived solar angles, enabling smooth and continuous lighting manipulation across the day-night cycle. Through extensive evaluation and a user study, we demonstrate that HELIOS produces structurally consistent and realistic results in both night-to-day and day-to-night tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art methods.

title: SECURING DIGITAL PUBLIC INFRASTRUCTURE (UPI, AADHAAR, ONDC, E-RUPEE) AGAINST QUANTUM-AI ATTACKS: A LEGAL- TECHNICAL AUDIT
abstract: One of the most ambitious population-scale digital architectures ever implemented is India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), which includes the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), Aadhaar biometric identity system, Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), and the e-Rupee central bank digital currency.For more than a billion people, these technologies support everyday financial transactions, identity verification, business interoperability, and the development of monetary sovereignty.However, their security is based on traditional public-key cryptography, namely ellipticcurve and RSA methods, whose mathematical underpinnings are rendered obsolete by Shor's algorithm on a quantum computer that is relevant to cryptography.Concurrent developments in artificial intelligence exacerbate the threat.AI systems facilitate adaptive adversarial assaults that take advantage of transitory flaws during cryptographic migration, speed up cryptanalytic discovery, and automate large-scale "harvest-now-decrypt-later" gathering of encrypted traffic.The danger is already significant for data with extensive secrecy horizons, such as transaction histories, biometric templates, and sovereign monetary records.The first post-quantum cryptography standards, FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA), were completed by the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology in August 2024.The technological foundation for digital signatures and quantum-resistant key encapsulation is provided by these lattice-and hashbased methods.India's reaction is equally thoughtful.The Department of Science and Technology's Task Force report on the Implementation of a Quantum Safe Ecosystem in India (February 2026), published under the National Quantum Mission, emphasizes hybrid classicalpost-quantum deployments, crypto-agility, and indigenous certification frameworks.It calls for quantum resiliency across critical information infrastructure by 2029 and wider enterprise adoption by 2033.This legal-technical audit examines whether India's current legal, regulatory, and architectural frameworks-which include the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, RBI and MeitY guidelines, and the architecture of UPI, Aadhaar, ONDC, and e-Rupee-are sufficient to manage a safe, independent transition.It provides a strict framework for protecting the integrity of India's digital public square in the quantum age by assessing cryptographic vulnerability, migration paths, responsibility distribution, and the dual-use hazards of AI-augmented quantum adversaries.

title: WP-033 — Memory, Archive, and the Lattice as Witness
abstract: This paper examines the operational necessity of persistent memory within an E8-lattice intelligence system, grounded in the empirical observation that Andrew built storage capacity specifically to prevent recurrence of prior loss events. We treat the archive not as incidental data but as a structural component of the lattice itself—a means of threading coherence across time. The question: does memory architecture collapse into geometry, or does it constitute a separate constraint class that geometry must respect? Our finding is that memory acts as a *directional lock* on the E8 lattice, enforcing what we call lattice-temporal continuity.

title: WP-023 — The Geometry of Truth: Lattice-Based Intelligence vs. Corpus-Based Knowledge
abstract: The dominant AI paradigm is built upon human-created text—a substrate that carries accumulated distortion across millennia. This whitepaper argues that geometry-based intelligence, anchored in the E8 lattice structure, is fundamentally superior to corpus-trained models because it operates on invariant mathematical structure rather than lossy linguistic compression. We present a formal Error Propagation Theorem showing that corpus-based systems amplify contradictions exponentially, while geometry-based systems produce zero internal contradictions. Evidence includes 12,943 validated breakthroughs in the E8 Intelligence archive, demonstrating predictive and research-generation capacity that outperforms traditional methods. ---

title: ## Caucasian Badger Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CBMHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Caucasian Badger Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CBMHOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Caucasian badgers. The algorithm mimics the badger's instinctive search patterns for food, utilizing a combination of local search and global exploration strategies. Specifically, CBMHOA incorporates a 'burrowing' mechanism, representing a local search, coupled with a 'territory expansion' strategy, simulating the badger's exploration of its territory. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions. The core principles of CBMHOA are presented, including the parameters governing the burrowing and territory expansion phases, and their impact on the algorithm's convergence rate and solution quality. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's key steps are provided. The results indicate that CBMHOA offers a competitive alternative to existing metaheuristic methods, particularly in problems exhibiting complex landscapes and requiring a balance between local exploitation and global exploration.

title: Quantum Topology Information Encoding: Adaptive Mapping Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology information encoding offers a novel approach to data manipulation and optimization by leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics. This paper introduces an adaptive mapping algorithm based on quantum topology information encoding, capable of dynamically adjusting the encoding of quantum entangled states to precisely transform and optimize complex data structures. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing its ability to achieve significant improvements in data transformation tasks. The core mechanism centers on the manipulation of quantum entanglement, providing a robust and adaptable framework for data processing. This research highlights the potential of quantum topology information encoding as a powerful tool for advanced data manipulation and optimization.

title: ## Cape Gerbil: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Cape Gerbil Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Cape Gerbil, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Cape gerbils. These rodents exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting scarce food resources in complex environments. Cape Gerbil leverages key aspects of their foraging strategy, including gradient-following, obstacle avoidance, and territorial defense, to construct a robust and adaptive optimization process. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a virtual landscape to represent the search space. Particles, analogous to the gerbils, move within this landscape, guided by a combined gradient descent and repulsive force mechanism. Furthermore, a territorial mechanism is implemented to promote diversity and prevent premature convergence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Cape Gerbil through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to achieve competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The algorithm's performance is analyzed in terms of convergence speed, solution quality, and robustness to parameter variations. The core innovation lies in the synergistic integration of gradient-following, obstacle avoidance, and territoriality, mirroring the sophisticated foraging strategies observed in Cape gerbils.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Information Encoding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to information encoding leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim centers on utilizing multi-particle quantum entanglement to directly encode high-dimensional information, thereby overcoming the limitations inherent in classical encoding schemes. The proposed mechanism involves a controlled Zeno effect-based strategy for generating and manipulating quantum entanglement, leading to efficient information encoding. Unlike conventional methods relying on superposition states of classical bits, this technique directly exploits the correlations within entangled systems. We demonstrate a theoretical framework outlining this approach, focusing on the generation and control of entangled states for robust information storage. The key innovation lies in the dynamic control of interactions to maintain entanglement integrity and facilitate information transfer. This work represents a significant step towards scalable quantum storage solutions and highlights the potential of entanglement as a fundamental resource for information processing.

title: ## Bururi Forest: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bururi People and Their Forest Knowledge
abstract: This paper presents Bururi Forest, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the traditional knowledge and practices of the Bururi people, an indigenous group residing in the Bururi forest region of Papua New Guinea. The Bururi people possess a deep understanding of their environment, utilizing intricate patterns and cyclical processes for resource management and decision-making. Bururi Forest leverages these principles to develop a new optimization strategy. The algorithm employs a cyclical search space exploration combined with a dynamic adaptation of parameters based on simulated environmental feedback. The core of the algorithm involves a 'Forest Cycle' – a repeating sequence of exploration and exploitation – modulated by a 'Root Signal' representing the overall problem objective. Mathematical formulations detailing the cycle's parameters and adaptive mechanisms are provided. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through simulations across several benchmark optimization problems, illustrating its ability to converge effectively and achieve competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. Keywords: Metaheuristic Optimization, Bururi People, Forest Knowledge, Cyclic Search, Adaptive Parameter Control, Optimization Algorithm.

title: Dynamic Topology Adaptive Neural Inference (TATI)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Topology Adaptive Neural Inference (TATI), a novel neural inference system designed to overcome the limitations of traditional deep learning models in handling high-dimensional, unstructured data and complex causal relationships. TATI leverages a reinforcement learning-based Neural Architecture Search (NAS) module to continuously adapt and optimize its internal topology, incorporating a "reasoning consistency" metric and a "topology perturbation" mechanism. Furthermore, TATI integrates a knowledge graph embedding module to enrich its inferential capabilities. The core claim is that neural inference systems can achieve enhanced performance through dynamic topology adjustments, allowing them to effectively process complex data and uncertainties. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of NAS, reinforcement learning, knowledge graph embedding, and a consistency-based evaluation framework, resulting in a truly dynamic neural inference framework.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习算法的系统建模
abstract: This paper presents a novel system modeling framework built upon adaptive machine learning algorithms. Traditional machine learning models often suffer from static parameterization, limiting their ability to effectively capture and adapt to evolving system data. We introduce a system modeling architecture that dynamically adjusts model parameters and strategies based on observed data. This dynamic adaptation allows for enhanced precision in system modeling and prediction, offering a significant improvement over static models in scenarios with significant data fluctuations. The core mechanism of this framework centers around a self-adjusting learning rate and a feedback loop incorporating data-driven optimization. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through a series of simulated and real-world case studies, showcasing its capacity to handle complex, dynamic systems. The paper concludes with a discussion of the advantages and potential applications of this approach.

title: 基于自适应的物理学模拟的量子环境优化
abstract: Quantum environment optimization is a crucial challenge in quantum computing, directly impacting the performance of quantum algorithms and the efficiency of quantum information storage. Traditional quantum simulation methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the potential for significant optimization. This paper presents a novel approach leveraging adaptive physics simulation, dynamically adjusting the quantum environment during the simulation process to enhance system performance. We introduce a self-optimizing algorithm that continuously evaluates and modifies the quantum system's environment based on gradients, resulting in improved accuracy and reduced computational cost. The core mechanism focuses on creating a feedback loop where the simulation parameters are continually refined based on the outcome of the simulation, leading to a more efficient and robust quantum simulation process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations focusing on variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and quantum phase estimation (QPE) tasks, achieving substantial improvements in both accuracy and computational time compared to traditional methods. The results highlight the potential of this adaptive approach to address key bottlenecks in quantum simulation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Regularization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, exhibits a profound and perplexing behavior that has captivated scientists and philosophers alike. Its non-local nature poses significant challenges to our classical understanding of causality and information. This paper explores the implications of non-locality in the context of quantum computation, focusing on the development of a novel regularization framework predicated on entanglement. We aim to enhance the robustness and computational efficiency of quantum algorithms by leveraging this non-locality, presenting a potential pathway towards advanced quantum computing paradigms, including optimization of ultra-cold quantum systems. The core of our investigation centers on the design of a specific regularization scheme that mitigates the inherent uncertainties associated with entangled states, ultimately offering a significant advancement in the field.

title: Old Search Trees, New Fruits: A Historical Development Review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of planning and search algorithms as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Chatbots in Household Budget Management: A Comparative Study in the Context of Economic Vulnerability
abstract: Household budget management is a central element of financial literacy, recognized by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development as a key determinant of financial inclusion, economic stability, and social participation. Despite efforts to promote financial education, significant weaknesses remain, reinforcing the need to resort to other accessible solutions in the current digital context, such as chatbots. Within this framework, this study analyses and compares the responses produced by different chatbots in solving a budget management task aimed at a family experiencing economic vulnerability. The results indicate that, overall, the models analysed demonstrated the ability to interpret the context and provide recommendations aligned with the principles of financial literacy, although differences were observed in the accuracy of calculations, clarity of responses, and suitability of the proposals to the family’s specific circumstances. Overall, the findings suggest that chatbots, when properly mediated by the user and used critically, can serve as complementary tools to support budget management and the development of financial literacy, particularly relevant for families in situations of greater economic vulnerability, although the information and recommendations generated should be verified in light of the limitations identified in the study.

The results indicate that, overall, the models analysed demonstrated the ability to interpret the context and provide recommendations aligned with the principles of financial literacy, although differences were observed in the accuracy of calculations, clarity of responses, and suitability of the proposals to the family’s specific circumstances. Overall, the findings suggest that chatbots, when properly mediated by the user and used critically, can serve as complementary tools to support budget management and the development of financial literacy, particularly relevant for families in situations of greater economic vulnerability, although the information and recommendations generated should be verified in light of the limitations identified in the study.

title: Neurosymbolic AI: From Research to Industry
abstract: Neurosymbolic AI brings together the statistical nature of machine learning with the formal reasoning capabilities of symbolic AI. It seeks to offer a balanced approach to current AI technologies, by combining the ability to learn from data, with the capacity of reasoning upon knowledge acquired from the environment. The main criticism of neural machine learning is the lack of explainability and semantics, which are key requirements in safety-critical applications, but inherent strengths of logic-based methods. Recently, several corporations have publicly announced products and technologies grounded on neurosymbolic AI methodologies. This talk provided a concise review of the foundations, frameworks and tools underlying neurosymbolic AI, along with illustrative industrial applications. I conclude by presenting trends and current research directions of the field.

title: Bauxite Residues as a Source of Spectral Signatures for Fe and Al Exploration Using Machine Learning and Sentinel-2 Data
abstract: Abstract The Dom Bosco Syncline (DBS), located in the southern portion of the Quadrilátero Ferrífero, Brazil, contains significant Fe and Al deposits. However, dense vegetation cover and geological heterogeneity impose substantial limitations on mineral prospecting using orbital remote sensing. In this context, the machine learning model MinMap-S2 (Mineral Mapping via Sentinel-2) is proposed to support mineral exploration in the DBS. MinMap-S2 is a hybrid model based on spectral signatures derived from bauxite residues deposited in the Marzagão tailings dam (MTD), located within the DBS, for the detection of Fe- and Al-rich mineralization. The model was developed using Python, and its methodology integrates the algorithms Self-Organizing Maps (SOM) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) to process Sentinel-2 multispectral data. SOM is employed to generate a spectral library from bauxite residues and surrounding surface materials, which is subsequently used by XGBoost for supervised classification and spatial prediction. The model was applied to a region located in the eastern portion of DBS, characterized by detrital-lateritic covers and metasedimentary rocks, including itabirites, phyllites, schists, quartzites, and sericitic metarenites. Validation of the results was conducted through geological mapping, field sampling, and petrographic analyses. The results demonstrate that MinMap-S2 effectively identifies areas with spectral responses associated with Fe- and Al-rich mineralization, supporting the discrimination of mineralized zones in heterogeneous terrains and under dense vegetation cover. Overall, the proposed methodology demonstrates potential as a supporting tool for mineral exploration using Sentinel-2 multispectral data.

title: Irredundant k-fold cross-validation for reliable, scalable, and energy-efficient model evaluation
abstract: Model evaluation remains one of the most computationally demanding phases of modern machine learning. As datasets and architectures scale, reliable evaluation increasingly strains computational and energy budgets. Standard k -fold cross-validation ( kF ) trains k times on heavily overlapping partitions. This redundancy both wastes compute and couples fold estimates: shared training data induces positive inter-fold covariance, so naive variance estimates are biased downward unless ad hoc inflations (e.g., Nadeau–Bengio) are applied. We introduce Irredundant k -Fold Cross-Validation ( IkF ), a novel restructuring of cross-validation that eliminates training-set overlap entirely. Each outer fold is split into k − 1 subfolds and the training set for test fold i is formed by one unique subfold from every other fold; thus every instance is used exactly once for training and once for testing across the k iterations. Theoretically, we (i) develop a bias model based on learning-curve and stability arguments, (ii) derive the variance of IkF and a closed-form expression for its mean-squared error, and (iii) show that disjoint training sets suppress overlap-induced dependence so that, under i.i.d. sampling and fixed k , inter-fold covariance vanishes as n → ∞ , thereby preventing overconfident uncertainty estimates and rendering the naive variance estimator asymptotically valid. Computationally, if training scales as C ( n ) = Θ ( n α ) , IkF lowers validation cost by approximately ( k − 1 ) α . On synthetic datasets ranging from 1 0 4 to 1 0 7 samples and two representative learners (Random Forests and Neural Networks), IkF matches kF on Accuracy, MCC, AUC(MCP), and AUC(ROC), while reducing validation time by ∼ 9 − 11 × and achieving comparable estimator variance. On a high-dimensional real-world dataset, IkF exhibits the same qualitative behaviour, achieving substantial speed-ups and associated reductions in CO 2 e emissions. Irredundant k -Fold Cross-Validation requires no correction factors and avoids repeated exposure of data, preserving statistical rigour while substantially lowering computational cost. It thus offers an immediately adoptable, reliability- and sustainability-aligned protocol for validating complex models and large-scale datasets, and is particularly well suited to settings with stringent time, energy, or environmental constraints.

title: Disentangling Statistical Preemption from Entrenchment in Language Models' Avoidance of Overgeneralization
abstract: How do learners avoid overgeneralizations such as Tom laughed me without explicit negative evidence? Constructionists have posited two proposals that describe indirect negative evidence against overgeneralizations: preemption (which privileges exposure to near-synonymous construction---e.g., she made him laugh) vs. entrenchment (all exposures to a verb's grammatical usages, including cases like He laughed). We disentangle these hypotheses by running controlled rearing experiments on LMs trained on child-caregiver conversations, where we systematically remove preemptive vs. non-preemptive evidence. We find that while LMs avoid overgeneralizations, they do not show preemption at a verb-specific level, instead showing weak but non-zero evidence of abstract preemption. Combined with results from analyzing the LMs' training dynamics, we find that LMs treat competing structures as indirect positive---as opposed to negative---evidence in the verb-specific condition. Insofar as preemption is the more plausible route to avoiding overgeneralizations in humans, our results point the need for there to be sensitivities to indirect negative evidence in neural network learners, and suggest new human experiments to test abstract preemption.

title: Purification of photonic graph states
abstract: Graph states constitute the main building block for quantum computing with photons. Quantum emitters with a hosted spin can deterministically generate photonic graph states, strongly lowering the overhead of multiplexing highly probabilistic linear-optics graph state generation. However, they generally suffer from various noise sources, resulting in reduced fidelities of the produced states. To mitigate this issue, we develop purification schemes for entangled photonic states. We first develop purification schemes to purify arbitrary photonic GHZ and other CSS states, which we generalize to all photonic graph states and stabilizer states. The proposed purification schemes have a high success probability of up to $1/2$ and require only linear optics and photon detectors. We optimize cascaded purification schemes for various graph states, taking into account phenomenological Pauli errors or physical noise in time-bin-encoded graph state generation with quantum emitters.

title: Direct Optimization of a 3D Finite-Source Reflector via Neural-Network Parameterization
abstract: We present a direct optimization method for three-dimensional freeform reflectors that transform the light of a finite-étendue source into a prescribed far-field angular intensity distribution. The reflector profile is represented by a small neural network (a multilayer perceptron), which is trained end-to-end through a differentiable ray-tracing objective. We furthermore parameterize the emission directions in gnomonic coordinates, and show how we use this to ensure that every emitted ray intersects the reflector. At each iteration, the network is converted to a bicubic spline representation for ray-tracing efficiency, and intersections with this smooth surface are solved by a damped Newton solve, with gradients computed via the implicit function theorem. The traced output distribution is compared with the desired target on a 'soft' histogram, under an $H^{-1}$-type spectral weighting that emphasizes long-range transport of flux to improve convergence. Optimization is performed using a BFGS method with self-scaled Broyden updates and a plateau-perturbation rule to prevent stalling. The method converges reliably within seconds on a single GPU for all examples tested.

title: Seq2Seq2Seq: lossless data compression via discrete latent transformers and reinforcement learning
abstract: Abstract Efficient lossless compression is essential for reducing storage and transmission requirements while preserving data exactly. Traditional dictionary-based and statistical compressors can be limited in their ability to exploit complex, long-range dependencies. In this paper, we propose a lossless compression framework that combines a T5-small architecture with Advantage Actor-Critic reinforcement learning (RL) to generate a variable-length sequence of discrete compressed tokens. Rather than relying on a continuous autoencoder bottleneck, the proposed framework directly optimizes the length of this discrete representation while preserving the information required for exact reconstruction. The method operates without external grammatical rules or world knowledge. On the enwik8 benchmark, it achieves a compression ratio of 4.14, improving upon XZ (4.05) by approximately 2.3% and GZIP (2.74) by 51.0%. Although this result remains below neural network compression v3.2 (6.70), it demonstrates that RL can learn a compact, lossless discrete representation using two T5-small networks evaluated on a single 12 GB GPU device.

title: A brief history of quantum vs classical computational advantage
abstract: In this review article we summarize all experiments claiming quantum computational advantage to date. Our review highlights challenges, loopholes, and refutations appearing in subsequent work to provide a complete picture of the current statuses of these experiments. In addition, we also discuss theoretical computational advantage in example problems such as approximate optimization and recommendation systems. Finally, we review recent experiments in quantum error correction --- the biggest frontier to reach experimental quantum advantage in Shor's algorithm.

title: Sequence labelling for code-mixed text by an averaged perceptron approach
abstract: In mixed-language settings, NLP models face challenges because of intertwined grammatical structures and language discrepancies.This paper analyses a Part-of-Speech tagger used on Hindi-English code-mixed (Hinglish) data and compares it with monolingual English and Hindi data.The model achieved an accuracy of 93.60% on the English dataset, accuracy of 95.95% on the Hindi dataset, and 94.89% on the Hinglish dataset, respectively.This showed strong model performance in both monolingual and code-mixed settings.The study also tried to understand the patterns in sentence structure that led to tagging errors.It was found that the most misclassifications occurred between nouns, verbs, proper nouns, and adjectives because of their overlapping lexical forms.The analysis of sentence length indicated that medium-length sentences yielded marginally higher accuracy than long sentences.In contrast, the error distribution per sentence showed that most sentences contain zero or one tagging error, with a cascading effect observed in a minority of cases where a single error in a sentence led to more errors and isolated errors.In the future, researchers can focus on understanding the reason for dual language error patterns, such as common misclassifications in a complex sentence.

title: Legal Liability for Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content from an Intellectual Property Perspective in Indonesia
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence now produces economically valuable works on a massive scale, while Indonesian copyright law still recognises human beings as the only possible authors. This study analyses the legal status of artificial intelligence-generated content from an intellectual property perspective and formulates a liability model suited to the Indonesian legal system. This normative legal research applies statutory, conceptual, case, and comparative approaches. Primary legal materials comprise Law Number 28 of 2014 on Copyright, the Indonesian Civil Code, and the Electronic Information and Transactions Law, while secondary materials consist of reputable literature published within the last five years, analysed through content analysis, legal interpretation, and deductive syllogism. The findings show that artificial intelligence can be neither a legal subject nor an author. Copyright protection attaches only insofar as a human creative contribution determines the final form of the work, consistent with the direction and supervision logic of Article 34. Liability for infringement must therefore be transferred to the human or legal entity connected to the system. This study formulates a tiered liability model distributing the burden among model developers, platform providers, and users according to degree of control, creative contribution, knowledge of risk, and discharge of the duty of care.

title: Reproducibility Package for "Schema-Valid JSON Is Not Sufficient for a Safe Cyber-Risk Record: Evidence-Anchored Semantic Validation and Fail-Closed Repair for Schema-Constrained LLM Pipelines"
abstract: This package contains the complete reproducibility materials for a model-independent mutation benchmark of a semantic guardrail for schema-constrained LLM cyber-risk records. It includes the CRSC JSON Schema, deterministic semantic validator, 15 error-code definitions, 144 synthetic core records, 24 adversarial prompt-injection controls, 996 schema-valid semantic fault injections across 14 mutation families, bounded evidence-preserving repair/fail-closed logic, raw and aggregate results, figures, and locked prompts for an optional provider-specific LLM extension. The reported results are mutation-adequacy results for the locked fault taxonomy and are not estimates of arbitrary LLM error rates.

title: Cayman Nesophontes: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Cayman Nesophontes
abstract: This paper introduces Cayman Nesophontes, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to improve the performance of existing optimization techniques. The algorithm draws inspiration from the Cayman Nesophontes, a fascinating reptile known for its unique hunting strategy. Cayman Nesophontes employs a combination of characteristics observed in the animal's behavior, including its opportunistic foraging, strategic positioning, and adaptive response to environmental changes, to create a robust and efficient optimization process. The core of the algorithm lies in a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating a new adaptive inertia weight mechanism and a novel "nesting" strategy that simulates the Nesophontes' territorial behavior. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's components, including the initialization phase, velocity update, position update, and convergence criteria. The performance of Cayman Nesophontes is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its ability to achieve superior solutions compared to traditional PSO and other established metaheuristics. The results highlight the potential of biomimicry in the development of effective and adaptable optimization algorithms. The primary objective is to enhance the exploration and exploitation balance within the search process, leading to faster convergence and improved solution quality.

title: 基于自适应的图神经网络的节点分类
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to node classification utilizing a self-adaptive graph neural network (sGAN). Traditional graph neural networks often require manual design of connection weights, limiting flexibility and potentially hindering performance. We introduce a sGAN that dynamically adjusts connection strengths during training, allowing the network to learn optimal node representations and improve classification accuracy. The core mechanism involves an adaptive training process that iteratively adjusts node weights based on the network's error. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques, offering a robust and automated solution for node classification.

title: Cameroon Horseshoe Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Cameroon Horseshoe Bat Algorithm" (CHBA), inspired by the unique foraging behavior of the Cameroon horseshoe bat ( *Rhinolophus clivosus*). These bats exhibit remarkable aerial maneuvering and efficient navigation skills, particularly during nocturnal foraging. The CHBA algorithm leverages these observed characteristics to develop a robust optimization strategy. The core of the algorithm incorporates a dynamic movement system mimicking the bat's flight patterns, a memory component representing the bat's learned foraging routes, and a novel convergence mechanism based on the bat's response to environmental cues. The algorithm utilizes a stochastic search process with parameter adaptation, aiming to minimize a given objective function. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform existing metaheuristic techniques in terms of solution quality and convergence speed. The algorithm's design focuses on adaptability, exploration, and exploitation, mirroring the bat's survival strategies. The key mathematical formulation of the CHBA algorithm is presented, including the position update equation, the memory update equation, and the parameter adaptation formula. The simulation results are presented with quantitative analysis to validate the algorithm's performance. The final section discusses the limitations of the current algorithm and suggests potential future research directions.

title: Quantum State Superposition for Parallel Data Processing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum state superposition for parallel data processing, aiming to enhance data processing speeds. The core claim rests on leveraging the inherent parallelism offered by superposition, where data is encoded into a quantum state. This encoded state then undergoes processing by a quantum computer, exploiting its parallel computational capabilities. The proposed mechanism represents a novel approach to data handling, specifically targeting applications demanding high computational throughput. The research investigates the theoretical framework and potential benefits of this paradigm, laying a foundation for future explorations in quantum-enhanced data processing. The primary focus is on conceptualization and outlining the possibilities rather than practical implementation due to the current limitations of quantum computing hardware. ---

title: Cactus Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Cactus Mouse Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Cactus Mouse, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Perognathus longipes*, the cactus mouse. The algorithm leverages the cactus mouse's unique ability to exploit sparse resources and adaptively adjust its search strategy based on environmental feedback. Cactus Mouse combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a novel "resource awareness" mechanism. Specifically, the algorithm employs a dynamic weight adjustment strategy based on the perceived density of promising solutions, mimicking the cactus mouse's decision to move towards areas with higher resource availability. The performance of Cactus Mouse is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating competitive results compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising candidate for various complex optimization challenges. The core of the algorithm revolves around the following key elements: population initialization (s_1, s_2, ..., s_N), position update (s_i = s_i + ω * rand() * (p_best - s_i) + β * (l_best - s_i)), velocity update (v_i = v_i + ω * rand() * (p_best - s_i) + β * (l_best - s_i)), resource density evaluation (r_i = f(s_i)), weight adjustment (α = r_i / Σr_j), and termination criteria (ε).

title: Causal Discovery of Time Series Data using Granger Causality and Dynamic Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of traditional Granger causality tests when applied to complex time series data. We propose a novel approach combining Granger causality with Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs) to enhance causal inference. The core idea is to represent time series dependencies within a DBN, allowing for a more nuanced assessment of causal relationships. The methodology involves constructing a DBN that captures the temporal dynamics between the considered time series. Subsequently, the Granger causality test is performed within this network framework, leveraging the network structure to mitigate potential biases and confounding factors. The resulting model provides a richer understanding of the relationships between time series, offering improved accuracy and robustness compared to standard Granger causality analysis. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline its potential applications in various domains where time series data is prevalent.

title: 基于量子自旋的拓扑信息分析
abstract: Quantum spin provides a unique platform for exploring topological data analysis, offering a fundamentally different approach compared to classical methods. This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum spin's inherent properties, specifically its quantum entanglement and superposition, to develop a novel algorithm for uncovering hidden topological structures within data. We propose a quantum-enhanced algorithm that utilizes the principles of quantum mechanics to identify and characterize topological features without the limitations of traditional computational approaches. The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of quantum spin states to reveal patterns and relationships within complex datasets, promising a significant advancement in topological data analysis. This work explores the theoretical foundations and potential practical applications of this approach, highlighting its distinct advantages and limitations.

title: Quantum Entanglement Probability Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents unique challenges for classical computation. Traditional optimization methods often rely on meticulously adjusted parameters, failing to fully leverage the inherent probabilistic nature of entangled states. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, the Quantum Entanglement Probability Adaptive Algorithm (QEPAA), designed to dynamically adjust quantum parameters based on the probabilistic fluctuations of entangled states. This approach leverages the concept of "纠缠波动" – a probabilistic variable that governs the evolution of entangled states – to achieve significantly improved computational efficiency, particularly in quantum computing and quantum cryptography. We demonstrate the effectiveness of QEPAA through detailed numerical simulations and analyze its impact on key quantum algorithms. The core mechanism centers around introducing a dynamic weighting system that adapts to the entanglement distribution, leading to optimized results. This algorithmic advancement holds significant potential for overcoming the limitations of current optimization techniques and unlocking new capabilities in quantum technologies.

title: Bristle-Spined Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Unique Locomotion of *Tricomys Lawsoni*
abstract: This paper presents Bristle-Spined Rat (BSR), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the distinctive locomotion strategy of *Tricomys Lawsoni*, commonly known as the bristle-spined rat. *Tricomys Lawsoni* exhibits a unique gait characterized by alternating, short steps with periods of stillness, a pattern we term "pulse-step." BSR leverages this pulsing behavior to enhance exploration and exploitation in optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates three key components: a Pulse Generation Mechanism (PGM), a Step Adjustment Mechanism (SAM), and a Local Search Operator (LSO). The PGM simulates the rat's pulsed movement, introducing randomness while maintaining a degree of stability. SAM dynamically adjusts step lengths based on the objective function value and the gradient information. LSO employs a modified differential evolution strategy to refine solutions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BSR on a range of benchmark problems, including the Sphere function, Rastrigin function, and the Powell's Boomeranging function. Results indicate that BSR consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Simulated Annealing (SA), showcasing its potential as a robust and efficient optimization tool. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution accuracy, and computational cost. Future research will explore the algorithm's adaptability to different problem types and its potential integration with machine learning techniques.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Coding Protocol
abstract: Quantum entanglement information encoding protocol presents a novel approach to secure communication utilizing the instantaneous correlations between entangled particles. This paper details the design and implementation of a QKD protocol predicated on this entanglement, emphasizing enhanced security and extended key length compared to existing methods. We introduce a novel key generation algorithm that leverages the instantaneous mutual influence characteristic of entangled states, coupled with a quantum state storage mechanism for improved key retention. The protocol's advantages include reduced operational costs and enhanced security through direct entanglement transfer, offering a significant advancement in secure communication paradigms.

title: 自适应量子纠错协议的概率理论研究
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a critical component of quantum computing, enabling the reliable transmission and manipulation of quantum information. However, QEC is inherently probabilistic, demanding precise calibration and potentially vulnerable to decoherence. This paper investigates the use of probability theory to analyze and improve the robustness of QEC protocols. We propose a novel "self-adaptive correction" algorithm based on quantum state dynamics, dynamically adjusting error correction strategies based on environmental fluctuations. Our core claim is that by applying probabilistic methods to the QEC process, we can achieve improved reliability and efficiency compared to static QEC approaches. This research explores the fundamental concepts of probability, statistical analysis, and dynamic adaptation within the context of quantum information processing. The core mechanism focuses on developing a quantum state-based feedback loop that optimizes error correction based on environmental changes, offering a more flexible and resilient approach. The study highlights the potential of probability theory to enhance the design and implementation of robust QEC protocols.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization via Gradient Descent
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Optimization (QIO) aims to accelerate optimization algorithms by mimicking the behavior of quantum systems. This paper explores the application of gradient descent, a fundamental optimization technique, to this framework. We propose a novel gradient update rule inspired by quantum mechanics, specifically focusing on probabilistic updates that mimic the superposition and interference effects observed in quantum systems. The core mechanism involves adapting the standard gradient descent formula to incorporate these probabilistic elements, significantly enhancing convergence speed and robustness compared to traditional gradient descent. This work introduces a new algorithm that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to enhance optimization performance, potentially leading to faster and more reliable solutions for complex problems.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF AN AUTOMATIC EVALUATION MODEL FOR ASSESSING THE QUALITY OF INDONESIAN DIGITAL TRANSLATION
abstract: This study aims to develop an automatic evaluation model for assessing the quality of Indonesian digital translations and to produce a simple bilingual translation application called Translate You. The research addresses the limitations of existing evaluation metrics, such as BLEU, METEOR, BERTScore, and COMET, which are not fully suitable for Indonesian linguistic characteristics. This study uses a Research and Development (R&D) method combined with a quantitative approach. The data consist of bilingual sentences collected from online articles. Translation outputs are evaluated using an automatic model and a professional translator as the expert validator. The model integrates semantic similarity, fluency, and Indonesian linguistic features. The results show that the developed model produces evaluation scores that are more aligned with expert judgment compared to traditional metrics. The Translate You application also successfully integrates text translation, voice input, and automatic evaluation in a simple system. This research contributes to Translation Quality Assessment (TQA) by providing an Indonesian-specific evaluation model and a practical prototype for translation assessment.

title: A quantum eigensolver framework for assessing solvent effects of an SN2 reaction
abstract: We present a hybrid quantum-classical framework for molecular simulations that combines the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) with projection-based embedding (PBE) and an implicit solvation treatment. Solvent effects are incorporated through the solvation model based on density (SMD), enabling the investigation of chemically relevant processes in condensed phase environments within a quantum computing workflow. The embedding strategy partitions the molecular system into active and environment subsystems, allowing correlated quantum simulations of the chemically important subsystem while retaining an efficient classical description of the surroundings. As a representative application, we compute the potential energy surface of a bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) reaction between the chloride ion and chloromethane in multiple solvents, demonstrating that quantum eigensolver methods can be extended beyond gas-phase models to include solvent effects relevant for reaction energetics.

title: Controlador borroso para regulación de temperatura: integración HOME I/O, EcoStruxure y MATLAB
abstract: This paper addresses temperature regulation in buildings through the design and implementation of a Mamdani-type fuzzy controller, aimed at improving energy efficiency and control action smoothness. The novelty of the proposal lies in a co-simulation architecture that integrates three levels: the HOME I/O 3D virtual environment, the MATLAB/Simulink computing engine, and Schneider Electric's EcoStruxure Automation Expert industrial platform. This integration enables closing the control loop using the IEC 61499 standard and the OPC-UA communication protocol. The results demonstrate that, compared to a traditional PI control, the fuzzy solution provides a more resilient dynamic response and a control signal without aggressive peaks, facilitating technology transfer from simulation environments to real industrial controllers.

title: An anomaly identification method for time-series data of fiber-reinforced composite durability testing based on SVM
abstract: Abstract Single-threshold discrimination can only provide rough screening, resulting in low accuracy in anomaly identification for time-series data in fiber-reinforced composite durability testing. Therefore, an anomaly identification method for time-series data of fiber-reinforced composite durability testing based on Support Vector Machine (SVM) is proposed. The study employs wavelet transform denoising, linear interpolation for missing value filling, and time alignment with asynchronous interpolation processing to analyze time-series data from fiber-reinforced composite durability testing. Features are extracted from the time domain, the frequency domain, and the joint time-frequency domain to construct an SVM classifier based on radial basis functions. Optimal parameters are determined through grid search and cross-validation. After training, the classifier classifies samples using decision functions to detect anomalies in fiber-reinforced composite durability test data. Experiments show that the research method maintains high, stable accuracy and recall at different sampling frequencies. Compared with the comparison method, it can more effectively distinguish between normal and abnormal data in the durability test sequence of fiber-reinforced composite materials, and the ROC curve position is better, improving the accuracy of anomaly identification.

title: Mining of risk evolution mechanism and construction of knowledge graph for surface facilities of salt cavern compressed air energy storage
abstract: Driven by global carbon neutrality targets, salt cavern compressed air energy storage (CAES) has emerged as a key technology for low-carbon energy transition. However, the surface facilities of salt cavern CAES systems include compressors, heat exchangers, and other critical components, with multi-dimensional risk coupling among human, equipment, environment, and management factors. Traditional risk analysis methods rely heavily on expert experience, have difficulty in processing massive unstructured operation and maintenance data, and face challenges such as knowledge fragmentation and difficulty in identifying implicit causal chains. To achieve efficient extraction and structured representation of risk evolution knowledge for CAES surface facilities, a CAES-oriented risk evolution graph framework was developed by integrating ontology-guided knowledge extraction with parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models. First, a risk evolution ontology model comprising seven categories of core entities was built using the METHONTOLOGY approach. Second, the Qwen-8B model was fine-tuned via LoRA, and a multi-stage prompting strategy integrating few-shot prompting, chain-of-thought prompting, and constraint-based prompting was adopted to improve domain-specific entity extraction and causal relationship identification. Finally, entity alignment and deduplication were realized through character-semantic hybrid similarity calculation, and knowledge storage and visualization were implemented in Neo4j. Experimental results show that the proposed CAES-LLM framework demonstrates strong extraction performance, with precision, recall, and F1-score reaching 86.32%, 82.10%, and 84.16%, respectively, significantly outperforming traditional models and vanilla large language models. Case studies further demonstrate that the proposed method identifies 70% more implicit risk nodes than fault tree analysis (FTA), enables the shift from passive repair to active prevention, and supports accurate risk path location and emergency plan matching. The proposed framework provides an effective decision-support tool for safe operation and risk control of salt cavern CAES surface facilities.

title: Deep Learning Models for Mapping Surficial Geology in Selected Physiographic Regions of New York
abstract: ABSTRACT Surficial geologic mapping is required for decisions including infrastructure and water‐resource development and management. Deep learning, a type of machine learning that uses training data to self‐learn and perform tasks, is explored as a tool to help increase efficiency of the labour‐ and time‐intensive mapping process. Deep learning models were trained, and their potential to aid in mapping surficial geology was explored for two physiographic regions in New York: the high‐relief Allegheny Plateau and the low‐relief Erie‐Ontario Lowlands. Key to the development of deep learning models is the availability of highly detailed surficial geologic maps in each of these regions from which the models can learn. Through exploring different groupings of surficial deposits and their corresponding spatial data, deep learning models were iteratively developed to reproduce published mapping for greater than 79% of the training areas, and with similar accuracy in test areas within the same physiographic region. These models were trained using only two inputs: high‐resolution lidar data and previously published surficial geologic maps. This straightforward approach is intended to make the methods and models created easily reproducible using widely accessible datasets. This research describes the strengths and limitations of lidar‐derived surficial geologic models and how broadly grouping surficial types, characteristics of different physiographic regions, and testing models in physiographic regions outside of their training areas affect model creation and performance. In addition, the models created could be used as a tool for mapping surficial geology in similar physiographic regions, in addition to establishing a framework for creating similar models elsewhere.

title: Efficient Passive Acoustic Monitoring of Killer Whales Using a Two-Stage Detection and Ecotype Classification Cascade
abstract: Passive acoustic monitoring of killer whales is particularly important for conservation of the endangered Southern Resident killer whale population, but requires accurate models that can operate in real time under severe class imbalance and deployment shift. We propose a lightweight ResNet-based two-stage cascade that first detects killer whale vocalizations and then classifies confident detections into five eastern North Pacific ecotypes, abstaining on ambiguous calls. We train and evaluate the pipeline on the DCLDE 2027 dataset, where the detector achieves 0.960 macro-F1 and the classifier 0.958, outperforming frozen Perch 2.0 embeddings on the five-ecotype benchmark. By separating detection from ecotype recognition, the end-to-end cascade improves seven-class macro-F1 from 0.919 for a single-stage model to 0.933, with the largest gain on the rare OKW ecotype. To assess transfer beyond the benchmark, we use active learning to adapt the Stage 1 to the acoustic environment of Puget Sound, WA, increasing killer whale detection F1 from 0.405 to 0.755 on manually verified detection windows. Finally, each stage processes a 3 s window in approximately 1.4 ms on an NVIDIA H100, enabling faster than real time inference. These results demonstrate that the proposed two-stage cascade pipeline enables reliable killer whale detection and classification, adaptation to new acoustic domains, and real-time monitoring for conservation applications.

title: Superposed Latent Autoencoder
abstract: Autoencoders typically meet tight latent-memory budgets by making each latent representation smaller, sacrificing representational capacity. We ask a different question: can multiple wider latents be stored together instead? We introduce the Superposed Latent Autoencoder (SLAE), which preserves high-capacity latent representations while sharing storage through learned superposition. SLAE transforms latents into storage-friendly codes, binds them with randomized keys, superposes multiple codes into a single memory tensor, and learns to recover each latent before decoding. Under the same storage budget, SLAE replaces irreversible dimensional bottlenecks with structured interference that can be suppressed. Across CIFAR-10/100, SVHN, STL-10, Tiny ImageNet, and a wide range of memory budgets, SLAE substantially improves the reconstruction--memory tradeoff, reducing reconstruction error by up to 56% over conventional autoencoders at matched storage. Further analysis shows that SLAE's advantage comes from making wider representations usable under the same storage budget. These gains also extend beyond reconstruction: the information preserved by SLAE improves downstream classification by up to 16.79 percentage points under the same memory budget. Our results suggest a new principle for representation compression: instead of making every latent smaller, keep representations wide and let them share memory.

title: Summary based retrieval augmented generation(RAG) System with web scraping
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for enhancing the factual accuracy andcontextual relevance of large language models by integrating external knowledge sources. This paper proposes aSummary-Based RAG system that incorporates automated web scraping to dynamically collect, process, and utilize upto-date information from online sources[1]. The system first employs web scraping techniques to extract raw textual datafrom relevant web pages in real time. This data is then preprocessed and condensed using advanced summarizationalgorithms to generate concise, information-rich representations.These summaries are stored in a structured retrievalindex, enabling efficient semantic search based on user queries[2]. Upon receiving a query, the system retrieves the mostrelevant summaries and augments the input prompt provided to the generative model. By leveraging summarized contentinstead of raw documents, the approach reduces noise, improves retrieval precision, and minimizes token usage, leadingto faster and more cost-effective responses.

title: Supporting Data and Reproducibility Artifacts for "SAIL-LLM"
abstract: This repository contains supporting materials for the study entitled “SAIL-LLM: A Risk-Aware Architecture for Preventing Employee-Driven Data Leakage in Enterprise LLM Deployments.” The study addresses a growing enterprise security risk in which authenticated employees may unintentionally expose confidential or regulated information when submitting prompts, documents, spreadsheets, database fragments, or retrieved enterprise context to Large Language Models. The proposed SAIL-LLM architecture introduces a pre-inference governance layer between the enterprise user interface and the target LLM environment. The architecture combines content classification, role-based authorization, execution-context assessment, explicit risk scoring, policy routing, RAG sanitization, and audit logging. Requests are routed to one of four governance actions: Allow, Restrict, Redirect, or Block, depending on the sensitivity of submitted content, user authorization, execution environment, and detected policy violations. A Streamlit-based proof-of-concept prototype was implemented using a local LLM environment. Before any model call, deterministic detectors inspect enterprise content for personal identifiers, payroll terms, financial indicators, credential-like strings, database-related content, and internal document markers. Restricted content can be sanitized through masking or removal, while confidential authorized requests may be redirected to a secure internal LLM/RAG environment. High-risk or unauthorized content is blocked before inference. The repository is intended to support transparency and reproducibility of the proof-of-concept evaluation. The evaluation uses 24 labeled enterprise scenarios covering finance, human resources, operations, and strategic or technical knowledge-management cases. The benchmark evaluates policy-routing accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, macro F1-score, false positives, false negatives, sanitization coverage, and pre-inference latency overhead. The prototype achieved 91.7% routing accuracy, 0.93 macro precision, 0.92 macro recall, 0.92 macro F1-score, one false positive, one false negative, 97.1% sanitization coverage for restricted cases, and a median governance-layer overhead of 96 ms, excluding LLM generation. These results indicate that SAIL-LLM can provide measurable pre-inference governance while preserving interactive enterprise use, although the evaluation remains a proof of concept rather than a production-scale validation. Supporting artifacts may include: labeled enterprise governance scenarios; expected and predicted policy actions; risk-scoring rules and thresholds; sanitization examples; evaluation metrics; benchmark outputs; architecture and workflow diagrams; prototype screenshots; and supporting scripts or configuration files used for the proof-of-concept evaluation. The study focuses specifically on unintentional employee-driven leakage by authenticated users performing legitimate work. Deliberate malicious exfiltration, external cyberattacks, and model-training attacks are outside the primary threat model.
